_doc: ADR-038 pinned consent map. The forbidden set is the real names that MUST NOT reach an E3/E4 (frontier) engine un-pseudonymized. Derived from IndrasNet core/config.REDACTION_MAP (tc-canonical-v1) + CONSENTED_FOR_BEDROCK_REDACT, EXTENDED with Chin/Aishwarya (ADR-038 finding 1.7: both were absent from every prior map). NOT yet auto-derived from the IndrasNet contacts external_llm_ok table — that sync is the documented follow-up; until then this file is the hand-pinned source of truth so the boundary is exercisable. 'data before claims'.
_owner_decision: owner_is_forbidden=true is the FAIL-CLOSED default: the owner's own name is pseudonymized before any frontier send, just like contacts. This is a flippable policy flag, surfaced for the owner's explicit decision (ADR-038 open question 6 / redesign finding 1.7 'owner handling explicit, not implicit'). Set to false if the owner consents to their own name leaving un-redacted.
_false_positive_note: Short first names ('Chin', 'Sahil') are common-word-shaped and may over-block legitimate redacted sends (whole-word, case-insensitive). For a privacy boundary, over-blocking (a refused send) is deliberately preferred over under-blocking (a real leak). Tune aliases per person as real identities are confirmed.
